name: Coffee Roast Log (Example)
author: @example-author
tagline: A template you can install, inspect, and replace.
summary: A reference community manifest for testing URL install and the local policy gate. It is a template for authors, not a validated roasting controller or a real product.
whatItIs: A protocol and a local log for recording roast batch context, tasting notes, and a same-array comparison against a reference bean. It helps a person keep a reproducible record of what changed.
whatItIsNot: Not a roast defect classifier, not a universal coffee identifier, not a concentration meter, and not a safety verdict. A pleasant aroma does not prove a batch is good, and a changed signal does not prove a defect.
citations: Example reference: replace this with a real paper or book. Author, year, title, venue. A citation is not decoration; it is the context for your claims.
Example reference: sensory analysis methods and the limits of a small, non-representative panel.

widgets.title: Coffee Roast Log (Example)
widgets.subtitle: A batch record with a sensor column, not a sensor verdict.
widgets.note: Community domain Vial · declarative · host-rendered · no executable code

widgets.headline: The roast is the evidence; the array is a prompt.
widgets.body: A roast can smell pleasant and still be under-developed, baked, or scorched. Record the charge weight, drop temperature, development time, and taste before you interpret the array.
always: Record the same bean, roast level, rest time, and grind before comparing two batches.
Use the same array and the same sample preparation for a same-rig comparison.
never: Do not turn a pleasant aroma into a quality score.
Do not compare a light roast on one array with a dark roast on another and call it a roast effect.

items.label: Signal
items.hint: Compare a batch against your own reference bean on the same rig.

items.label: Context
items.hint: The log is the primary evidence; the array is one column.

items.label: Not a
items.hint: No defect classification and no universal coffee ID.

widgets.title: Roast log
widgets.description: Keep the context fixed enough that a comparison means something.

rules.when: The log context changed (bean, roast level, rest day, or grind)
rules.then: Do not compare the reading to the old baseline. Record a new reference on the same array.

rules.when: The aroma is pleasant but the primary roast measurements are outside your recipe
rules.then: Treat the batch as a process question, not a successful roast. The array does not clear it.

widgets.title: Use this with your rig
widgets.body: Capture a reference and a sample on the same array. If the channel sets differ, Check refuses the comparison. The export is a manifest, not a model.

docs.title: How to use this workspace
body: Record the bean, roast date, roast level, and rest day before the first reading.
Capture a reference sample and a batch sample on the same array, then compare them in Check.
Write down what you tasted. The log is the primary record; the array is a prompt to look.

docs.title: What it cannot tell you
body: It cannot tell you whether a roast is objectively good, defective, or safe.
It cannot identify a coffee variety or origin from an aroma.
It cannot transfer a result from one rig to another without a calibration story.

docs.title: References
body: Replace the example citations with real sources. Cite the method and the domain claim, not just the idea.
The references contextualise the workspace. They do not validate the sensor or the local array.
